## UX Copy Review: Tova M1 landing page

**Scope:** every visible string, plus the accessible names and alt text in `site/index.html`, and the messages generated by `site/js/main.js` (errors, loading, modals). Taken from the live page at localhost:4322, after five rounds of fixes.

**Voice:** `brand.md` asks for "warm, plain English. No jargon, no ALL CAPS shouting", sentence case, and `$1,690`.

**User state:** a sceptical parent deciding whether to put down $99 on a phone, often in the evening (see `04-ux-discovery.md`).

**Result: 41 findings.**
- 🔴 7 block or mislead
- 🟡 19 hurt clarity or trust
- 🟢 15 polish

Already good, from earlier rounds: one price, date and deposit everywhere; a single "Reserve for $99" action; plain-language form errors and hints; a confirmation modal that says what happens next; and the three reassurance blocks from `05-ux-copy.md`.

> **Update (decision: free waitlist).** #1 is fixed with option C:
> - every CTA now reads "Join the waitlist" ("Join →" in the mobile header);
> - every "$99" and "deposit" mention is gone;
> - the order band, FAQ (#7), peace-of-mind row, loading state ("Joining…") and confirmation ("You're on the list") are rewritten to match.
>
> #4 now reads "8,400 people on the waitlist so far". It still has to come from live data. The other findings are still open.

---

### 🔴 Critical: these block or mislead

| # | Element | Current | Issue | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Form CTA + confirmation | "Reserve for $99 →" → modal "Your Tova is reserved" | **The form never takes a payment.** It asks only for an email and a ZIP code, then says the robot is reserved. Either the $99 is never charged, or the confirmation is false. This is the biggest trust breaker on the page | If payment comes next: button **"Continue to payment →"**, then a payment step, then "Your Tova is reserved". If it really is a free waitlist: button **"Join the waitlist"**, and drop "$99" from every CTA |
| 2 | Hero subtitle | "The most capable home robot for $1,690" | An unprovable superlative ("most capable"), which is a legal and credibility risk. It also says nothing about what the robot does | **"Tidies up, loads the dishwasher and folds laundry. $1,690."** (see alternatives) |
| 3 | Cookie banner | "We use cookies to improve your experience and for marketing. By continuing to browse you agree." · "reject" / "Accept all cookies" | "By continuing you agree" isn't valid consent under GDPR, and is risky under US state privacy laws. Lowercase "reject" vs title-like "Accept all cookies" nudges people. It also contradicts "We never sell your data" in the privacy block | **"We use essential cookies to run this site. With your OK, we'll also use cookies to measure visits and improve our ads."** · Buttons **"Accept all"** / **"Essential only"** (equal weight) + a **"Cookie settings"** link |
| 4 | Social proof | "8,400 people have already reserved." | A specific number that must be true, and kept up to date. If the form doesn't take a deposit (#1), they didn't "reserve" | Show it only if it comes from live data. Wording: **"8,400 reservations so far"** (a fact, not pressure) |
| 5 | Footer email | "hello@" → `mailto:` (empty) | A broken contact, on the only "Contact us" destination | **"hello@tova.example"** with a real `mailto:`, or a **"Contact us"** link to a form |
| 6 | "Contact us" (header) | Jumps to the footer | The label promises a way to contact you. The footer has no contact method (see #5) | Point it to a contact page or form, or rename it **"Help"** and link to the FAQ |
| 7 | FAQ "Can I cancel?" | "…refunded in full. See terms." | "See terms" isn't a link. It also ignores the new 30-day home trial, so cancellation before and after delivery are confused | **"Yes. Before your Tova ships, cancel anytime from your confirmation email and get your $99 back. After delivery, you have 30 days to send it back for a full refund. [Read the full terms]"** |

### 🟡 Major: these hurt clarity or trust

| # | Element | Current | Issue | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | H1 | "TOVA M1" (typed in caps) | Screen readers may spell it out ("T-O-V-A"). The brand says no ALL CAPS | Type **"Tova M1"** in the HTML, and use CSS for caps if wanted |
| 9 | Spec titles | "APP", "ARMS", "LIDAR", "CAMERAS", "AUDIO", "BATTERY", "ASSEMBLY" (typed in caps) | Same issue: "APP" can be read as letters. ALL CAPS shouting | **"App", "Arms", "Lidar", "Cameras", "Audio", "Battery", "Assembly"** (CSS can still style them as labels) |
| 10 | Spec: arms | "7+1 DOF, 1.5kg payload per-arm" | Jargon (DOF, payload). The explanation is hidden in a hover tooltip. "per-arm" shouldn't be hyphenated. No space in "1.5kg" | **"Two 7-joint arms with grippers. Each lifts up to 1.5 kg (3.3 lb)."** |
| 11 | Spec: lidar | "12m range, 8–12Hz" + tooltip "Angular resolution 0.72° at 10Hz." | Numbers without a benefit. The tooltip adds more jargon | **"Maps rooms up to 12 m (40 ft) across, so it never bumps into furniture."** Remove the tooltip, or make it "Scans its surroundings 10 times a second." |
| 12 | Spec: cameras | "4× 720p RGB, 30fps" | Jargon. It doesn't say where the cameras are, which matters for the privacy story | **"4 HD cameras, on its hands, head and neck."** |
| 13 | Spec: audio | "Speaker + far-field mic" | Jargon, and a symbol instead of "and" | **"A speaker and microphone, so you can talk to it."** |
| 14 | Spec: battery | "6–8 hrs" | Abbreviation, and no context | **"6–8 hours per charge. Back to full in 2.5 hours."** |
| 15 | Task captions | "Unloading groceries, 0.8x speed" | Ambiguous: is the video slowed down, or is the robot slower than a person? | **"Unloading groceries · shown at real speed"** (or "sped up 2×", whichever is true) |
| 16 | Tasks intro | "Tova can support you with day-to-day home tasks, so you can get back to the things you actually like doing." | "Can support you with" is weak and vague. "Actually" sounds slightly condescending | **"Tova takes care of the everyday chores, so you get your evenings back."** |
| 17 | Task names | "Helping in the kitchen" next to specific ones ("Loading dishes") | The vaguest label comes first and overlaps with "Loading dishes" and "Pouring ingredients" | **"Unloading groceries"** (it matches its caption) |
| 18 | Nav | "Product" → the tasks section | The label doesn't match the destination | **"What it does"** (or "Tasks") |
| 19 | Marketplace link | "click here to see all skills" → `#` | "Click here" isn't descriptive, it's lowercase, and it goes nowhere | **"Browse all skills →"**, linked to the marketplace (or removed) |
| 20 | Compare columns | "Competitor A", "Competitor B" | Unconvincing, and it reads as if something is hidden | Name categories: **"Robot vacuum"** ($499-ish) and **"Research robot"** ($24,000). Or name real products, after a legal review |
| 21 | Compare: offline | "Works offline ✗" with no note | It reads as a red flag, and seems to contradict "what it sees stays home" | Row: **"Works without internet"**. Cell: **"Partly"** + a note: "Navigation and built-in tasks work offline. New skills and the app need internet." |
| 22 | Compare: price | "$24k" vs "$1,690", "$4,999" | Inconsistent number format | **"$24,000"** |
| 23 | Press quote | "Tova feels like the iPhone moment for robots." | A cliché, and a trademark comparison. The quotes have no dates or links, so they're hard to trust | Replace it with a specific quote (what it did, in which test), and add the date and a link for each outlet |
| 24 | FAQ "Does Tova need the internet?" | "Core navigation runs on-device. Skills and the Studio app require an account and an internet connection." | "On-device" is jargon. It doesn't mention the built-in tasks | **"Not for everyday use. Getting around your home and the 6 built-in tasks work offline. You'll need internet and a free account for the app and new skills."** |
| 25 | FAQ "Is it safe around kids and pets?" | Repeats the trust block in shorter form | It duplicates the trust block, and the two could drift apart | **"Yes. Its arms stop on contact and it moves slower than walking pace. [See how Tova keeps your home safe and private]"** (link to #safety) |
| 26 | App name | "Tova app" (privacy block) vs "Tova Studio app" (included list, marketplace, specs, FAQ) | The same thing has two names, or it's two apps and nobody says so | Pick one name. If it's one app: **"Tova app"** everywhere, "Studio" being a mode. Confirm with product |

### 🟢 Minor: polish

| # | Element | Current | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|
| 27 | Eyebrow | "// reservations open · ships Q1 2027" | Drop the code-comment "//": **"Reservations open · Ships Q1 2027"** |
| 28 | CTA arrows | "Reserve for $99 →" | Wrap "→" in `aria-hidden` so screen readers don't say "right arrow". Keep it visually |
| 29 | Mid-page summary | "$1,690 total · ships Q1 2027 · refundable until it ships" | **"$1,690 total · $99 deposit, refundable · Ships Q1 2027"**. It's the deposit that's refundable, not the price |
| 30 | Pause control | "Pause" / "Play" | **"Pause" / "Resume"**. "Play" suggests a video |
| 31 | Skill prices | "FREE", "free", "$1.99/mo" | **"Free"**, **"Free"**, **"$1.99/month"** |
| 32 | Skill meta | "4.8 ★ · 2.1k installs" | Add a hidden "rating" label (★ is read as "black star"). Use one number style: "2,100 installs", "11,000 installs" |
| 33 | Section label | "Skills Marketplace" | **"Skills marketplace"** (sentence case, like every other label) |
| 34 | Specs label + title | "Affordable and capable" · "Hardware that punches above its price." | The label is generic. The title is an idiom that's hard to translate. **"Inside Tova"** · **"Serious hardware, home-friendly price."** |
| 35 | Spec: app | "…helps you train, operate, and manage your robot." | Serial comma: the rest of the page doesn't use one. **"…train, control and manage your robot."** |
| 36 | Press citations | "THE CIRCUIT" (typed in caps) | Type **"The Circuit"**, styled with CSS |
| 37 | Cart modal | "Your cart" / "Your cart is empty." | Empty-state pattern (what + why + next): **"Nothing in your cart. Tova M1 is available to reserve. [Reserve for $99]"**. Better: remove the cart icon until there's a store |
| 38 | Success modal | No action button, only "×" | Add a **"Done"** button, and a line about the next step: "We'll email you before your Tova ships." |
| 39 | Task image alt | "Tova helping in the kitchen: Unloading groceries…" | Lowercase after the colon: "…: unloading groceries" (lowercase the caption in the script) |
| 40 | Footer | "© 2025 TOVA ROBOTICS INC." · "Privacy", "Terms" → `#` | **"© 2026 Tova Robotics Inc."** · **"Privacy policy"**, **"Terms of sale"**, real links |
| 41 | Form | No privacy note under the email field | **"We'll only email you about your reservation."** (+ an optional, unticked "Send me product updates" checkbox) |

### Key rewrites with alternatives

#### Hero subtitle (#2)
**Recommended:** Tidies up, loads the dishwasher and folds laundry. $1,690.

| Option | Copy | Tone | Best For |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| A | Tidies up, loads the dishwasher and folds laundry. $1,690. | Concrete, confident | Default. Leads with the jobs Maya cares about |
| B | The home robot that does the chores you hate. $1,690. | Warm, emotional | Social ads and campaigns |
| C | Two arms, six everyday chores, $1,690. | Short, factual | Narrow screens, press kit |

#### Cookie banner (#3)
**Recommended:** "We use essential cookies to run this site. With your OK, we'll also use cookies to measure visits and improve our ads." · [Accept all] [Essential only] · Cookie settings

| Option | Copy | Tone | Best For |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| A | We use essential cookies to run this site. With your OK, we'll also use cookies to measure visits and improve our ads. | Plain, honest | Default, with equal-weight buttons |
| B | Cookies help us see what's working on this page. Essential ones are always on, the rest are up to you. | Friendly | If there's no ad tracking at all |
| C | This site uses cookies. Choose which ones you allow. | Minimal | Strict-consent regions, with a settings panel |

#### Form CTA (#1): pick the one that matches what really happens
| Option | Button | Confirmation title | Best For |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| A | Continue to payment → | (after paying) Your Tova is reserved | A real $99 deposit, with a payment step |
| B | Reserve for $99 → (and a card field in the form) | Your Tova is reserved | Payment collected in the same form |
| C | Join the waitlist | You're on the list | No money taken now. Remove "$99" from every CTA |

### Rationale
- **Truth before tone.** The three critical issues that matter most (#1 payment, #2 superlative, #3 cookies) are about saying what really happens. On a page that asks for money and promises privacy, one false or coercive line undoes the whole trust section.
- **Benefits over specs for Maya, specs one tap away for Daniel.** Rewriting the spec values in plain words (#10–14) keeps the numbers but leads with what they mean at home.
- **Consistency closes the last gaps.** One app name, one number format, sentence case typed in the HTML (with CSS for styling). These are cheap fixes that make the page feel finished.
- **Accessible names are copy too.** Text typed in caps, "click here", the arrow characters and the ★ all affect what screen-reader users hear.

### Localization Notes
- **Idioms to replace before translating:** "punches above its price", "extra pair of hands", "Not the right fit?", "the iPhone moment".
- **Units:** pair metric with imperial for the US (kg/lb, m/ft, m/s/mph), and show only metric elsewhere.
- **Dates:** "Q1 2027" is business jargon in some markets. Consider "early 2027" for consumers.
- **US-only content:** ZIP code, UL 3300, the financing wording and "anywhere in the US" all need local equivalents.
- **Cookie consent:** wording is a legal requirement that varies by region (opt-in in the EU and UK, opt-out notices in some US states). Have legal approve each version.
- **Voice command:** "Tova, stop listening" stays in English unless the robot understands it in the target language.
- **Text expansion:** labels on pill buttons ("Reserve for $99 →") grow by 30–40% in German and French. Check that the mobile header still fits (it already shortens to "Reserve →").

### Update: all remaining findings applied (2026-11-12)

Every finding from #2 to #41 is now in `site/index.html`, `site/js/main.js` and `site/css/styles.css`, with the free-waitlist framing kept throughout.

- **Critical:** benefit-led hero subtitle (#2). Honest cookie banner, with equal-weight "Essential only" / "Accept all" buttons and a "Cookie settings" link (#3). A real footer email (#5). "Contact us" is now "Help" and links to the FAQ (#6).
- **Major:**
  - The H1, spec titles and press names are typed in sentence case, with caps applied in CSS (#8, #9, #36).
  - The specs are plain-language benefits with metric and imperial units (#10–#14).
  - Captions say "shown at real speed" (#15). New tasks intro and nav labels (#16–#19).
  - Named competitor types, "Partly" offline support with a note, and "$24,000" (#20–#22).
  - A specific press quote (#23). Clearer FAQ answers, with a link to #safety (#24, #25).
  - The app is called "Tova app" everywhere (#26). 🔶 Product needs to confirm the name.
- **Minor:**
  - Decorative arrows are hidden from screen readers (#28). Pause/Resume (#30).
  - Consistent prices (#31). Star ratings get a hidden "rating" label, and install counts are written out in full (#32).
  - New section labels and copy (#33–#35).
  - The cart empty state has a call to action (#37). "Done" button in the confirmation (#38).
  - Lower-case image alt text (#39). Footer legal links and year (#40).
  - Privacy hint under the email field, plus an unticked opt-in for product updates (#41).
- **Checked in the browser:** no horizontal overflow at desktop or 375px. Cart → waitlist, form → confirmation → Done, and Pause/Resume all work. A rescan found none of the old strings.
